invariants.why: One WebSocket JSON-RPC client is shared by every page. A second transport, or a rename, must be declared here deliberately rather than absorbed by the graph.
Every calling surface competes for the same pool and socket. A surface that reaches the gateway some other way breaks the concurrent-access picture the graph draws.

The pool is the transport's only shared mutable state: every mutation happens under the lock, continuations resume and frames are written outside it. The critical-section assembly assumes exactly this shape.
If the register, resolve or remove rules stop matching the source, the pool must fail the build rather than look idle.
Sections are assembled per enclosing function; an operation with no resolved scope would silently drop out of its section.
Every namespace box is dispatched by a transport core; a namespace reached any other way is a new construction, not a variant of this one.
Every store the extractor recognises is a construction on the map, so the System map can never disagree with the extractor about what holds state.

Every page's views drive at least one surface through an observed action or lifecycle hook. SwiftUI has many ways to attach an action; if a refactor hides them from the rules, the first hop must fail loudly rather than vanish.

The App entry points construct the objects that exist before any page: the settings object reads the keychain in its initialiser and is what the transport connects with. A store read only at launch belongs to the launch zone, not to the shared core; if the @StateObject or init rules stop matching, launch must fail loudly rather than dissolve into shared.

An object's lifecycle is the enum its stored state property is typed with, and every state must be reachable by an assignment somewhere in the type. Adding, renaming or orphaning a state changes the construction and must be declared here in the same change; a state nothing ever enters is dead code the map would otherwise draw as live.

A system flow is a path over edges the map draws, never a diagram beside it. When the construction changes under a flow, the flow must be updated in the same change rather than quietly describing wiring that no longer exists.
Every declared page owns at least one construct. An empty page means its roots or ownership declarations have drifted from the source.
